name: wget
summary: Download files from the web, within the web access the application allows
help: Download each URL to a file named after it (or as -O says), following redirects.
-O,  --output-document=FILE   write to FILE; '-' writes to standard output
-q,  --quiet                  print nothing but errors that end the run
--post-data=STRING       send STRING in a POST body
--post-file=FILE         send FILE in a POST body
--no-check-certificate   accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified
The application decides which sites can be reached; others fail like an unknown host.

options.description: write every response body to FILE ('-': standard output)
print each response's status line and headers on standard error
send a POST with STRING as its body
send a POST with FILE's contents as its body
time limit for each request (the policy's limit still applies)
the most redirects to follow (never more than the policy allows)
accepted and ignored: certificates are always verified

exitCodes.1: generic error (an output file that cannot be written, a request the web policy refuses)
exitCodes.4: network failure: host not resolved or not allowed, connection refused, timeout
exitCodes.8: the server answered with an error status, or too many redirects

messages.resolve: wget: unable to resolve host address {host:locale}
messages.timeout: Read error (Connection timed out) in headers.
messages.recv: Read error (Connection reset by peer) in headers.
messages.tooLarge: wget: the response is larger than the web policy allows ({limit} bytes)
messages.blocked: wget: blocked by the web policy: {reason}
messages.replay: wget: Topwater replay: {request} is not in the recording

notes: Registered in every shell; without a web policy every host fails to resolve. The progress report is shortened: no Resolving/Connecting lines, no dots or speed. No retries.
